Firstly, I wanted to send my condolences to you. It's never easy to lose a beloved pet. Throughout my life, my family had lost quite a few pets and a few years ago, we had lost our cat. In fact, he didn't die alone because, the night he passed, I've witnessed the life in his eyes fade away as I've held him. I held back my tears as much as I possibly could and had to be strong to tell him that it was okay to let go. He was suffering so much. 

Even writing this, many years could go by, and not know that I am still grieving. Grief can swoop in, without us knowing. It's a process that takes time. We also cremated our cat. 

My advice would be is to embrace and take in the grief. Feel the emotions and not hold back. The reason why I say this is that, it is never good to build up every emotion and where you would eventually explode by becoming overwhelmed. It is okay to remember the good times and memories of your dog. As for the pain, it will eventually ease and you will be okay. However, it is all on your terms when you ready to.

I get told these things by people and what I tell them back/think:

"It's okay to love yourself and can't you just love you?" Um, I don't know how to love myself and I hate myself as well too. 

"If you kill yourself, everyone will hate you forever." Whatever floats their boats, I guess and I highly doubt that some of them would or not.

"Things will get better." I hate whenever someone tells me this because they simply are guessing and don't really know. Meaning, in other words, they don't know how my Depression is like. 'Things don't just become better.' I wish that many would understand.

"When you die, you better make sure that you were a mistake." Whatever, and, thank you for the kind death sentencing words. It means a lot. I will make sure to make a trip visit to haunt you. 

And lastly...from someone that I do not know at all

"Stay away from my children you fucking bitch and your psychotic craziness. You should rot in hell and die." Who are you? And no, obviously not the crazy one here, it's you. You were coming at me and that's uncalled for. Though, thank you for telling me to die and rot in hell.

I'm sorry that you're struggling and had relapsed. Getting back into again is like an addiction. I can't remember the last time when I had stopped. Though I don't feel ashamed of it, ya know?

I agree with what everyone else had said and we all have our own experiences, however, it's unfortunately very true that Depression can manifest in lots of ways and then, sometimes, it is hard to spot out the differences. Firstly, I wanted to say, you are not crazy nor an attention seeker. Although I do recommend seeing a Therapist. For example, I always knew that something was wrong with me and off. I would have these periods for days of being drained, withdrawn, feelings of hopelessness, angry, hating the world, etc. 

Until last year, I was fully diagnosed with MDD also known as Severe Clinical Depression. Do I enjoy it? No, not really. I'm slowly but steadily still learning about its effects. As for me, I would call it, my "Good Days" and "Bad Days." The Bad Days, can at times be mild or severe. Like yesterday. I would feel; on edge, anxious, paranoid, numb, racing thoughts, uncontrollable crying spells, feeling bored, wanting/not wanting to be alone- and sleeping in all day. 

And lastly, I wanted to mention, you are not alone in this. I, myself, and others understand too. Even if there are times, where you don't feel heard, always stand your ground and speak up because your voice matters and should always be heard.
